workItems.conclusion: Notebook classified into 24 product requirements, 20 engineering rules, 12 NFRs, 20 architecture decisions, 6 hypotheses, 18 risks, 30 open questions and 10 non-goals. Two spikes run; parser selected; scope-resolution false-edge risk discovered. 12 implementation work items created with traceability.

Live PostgreSQL 16.15 comparison run. PostgreSQL resolves a CTE-shadowed name to the CTE, confirming DF-STRATA-2026-9B2E against the real engine; it refuses ambiguous columns and folds unquoted identifiers, both matching Strata's model. Demonstrated RK-003: the 17.5 parser accepts JSON_TABLE and MERGE...RETURNING which the 16.15 server rejects, so a statement can be reported as parsed while being unexecutable. Recorded as a gap for the S4 validation slice. Overload resolution and Q-027 remain untested.

Spike D context-cost half run with its own harness, since ROS telemetry reports token capabilities as unsupported here. 46x-101x context reduction at 200 tables, 2.4x at 4 tables: raw context is O(schema size), a Strata point query is O(1). HY-STRATA-2026-1E5D moves to supported at medium confidence, held at medium because the baseline assumes an agent reads the whole schema rather than grepping selectively. Secondary finding: the scope-and-caveats block is larger than the result for point queries and is repeated verbatim per answer; emitting it once per session would cut a multi-query session by roughly two thirds. The correctness half (HY-STRATA-2026-2A6F) was NOT run - no agents were executed - and is recorded as untested.

Nine-task information-sufficiency evaluation found Strata insufficient on 3 of 9 where raw DDL was sufficient: inspect omitted unique constraints, check constraints and indexes, all already in the model and populated by introspection but never rendered. Fixed; now 9/9. Repair cost ~141 tokens across 7 tasks (ratio 2.4x to 2.3x), establishing that the context reduction reported in EV-STRATA-2026-F4C6 is genuine rather than an artefact of dropping data. Task set was author-written, which biases toward questions Strata answers well; only inspect was probed in depth. Still not agent correctness.

Six agents, three per condition, identical graded task set. NULL RESULT: 15/15 correct in both conditions, no difference detected, and the Strata condition used 8.7% more tokens. Ceiling effect - an 8KB context is small enough that a capable agent misses nothing, including the designed discriminator. HY-STRATA-2026-2A6F tested and not supported, remains proposed rather than rejected. HY-STRATA-2026-1E5D qualified: it holds for large schemas with targeted queries and is actively false for small schemas with pre-fetched sessions. The crossover schema size is now the largest decision-relevant unknown.

Cross-module seam experiment broke the ceiling that defeated the earlier lookup test. Two of five tasks discriminated in OPPOSITE directions: raw 3/3 and Strata 0/3 on column-level impact (T1, a capability gap - no column-level reader query); Strata 3/3 and raw 0/3 on cross-module unenforced relationships (T5, where raw agents conflated dependency with relationship and over-reported). HY-STRATA-2026-2A6F is too coarse as stated: correctness depends on which seam question is asked. T1's gap is the highest-value fix the experiment found.

Tested at 3,009 files / 2.37M tokens with both conditions interactive. The advantage does NOT survive: grep answered the discriminating question in 15ms against Strata's 247,000ms, and both raw agents answered all four seam questions correctly including the SELECT * case designed to be Strata-only. The small-scale relationship-typing win did not reproduce. Three problems identified: no corpus-wide seam query (relationships is per-object, so finding unknown seams needs 200 invocations), no cached index, and a scope block that was 330x the answer until bounded. Fixed the packaging; the other two are open.

Built the messy fixture: unqualified names, three schemas sharing a table name, alias-only references, SELECT *, CTE shadowing, comment noise, dynamic SQL. It did NOT discriminate - both agents scored 6/6 recall and 6/6 precision, identical to Strata, rejecting every trap with accurate reasons. HY-STRATA-2026-2A6F moved to rejected after four regimes and thirteen agent runs. The fixture did find a real Strata bug: columnDependencies used the catalog-BLIND resolver, so every bare-name column reader was silently dropped whenever more than one schema was on the search_path. Fixed with scope resolution still running first to preserve RK-001, plus three regression tests including an ambiguity control.

Five decision records written, DF-STRATA-2026-A4D9 marked superseded in part, roadmap updated, and WI-0078..WI-0089 captured. The rejected alternatives are recorded alongside the conclusions — Strata generating SQL, and signing each source file — because both were proposed seriously and the reasons against them are the load-bearing part. One finding from checking rather than assuming: DF-STRATA-2026-5E9F documents that the gate currently promotes a clean corpus scan into an Allow verdict for DropTable, which contradicts the analysis-scope discipline the rest of the codebase enforces.
